text:
Wyatt Johnston scored 45 goals last season. This season he has five in 18 games on 9.1 expected goals. He keeps getting the looks: 1.55 expected goals per 60, higher than last year, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 93rd percentile for chances from the slot. Goals tend to follow chances like that.

He's still producing. He has 18 points, 10 of them on the power play, and goals in two straight games, including a power play insurance goal against Florida. He's shooting 10% against a talent range centred near 16%, and our numbers still project about 30 goals.

The question mark is defensive. Evolving-Hockey had opponents generating more against him than against all but 12% of forwards last season, and Dallas is only slightly better with him on the ice at five on five this year (52.6% of the expected goals). What to watch: the five-shot, 1.32 expected goals night against San Jose came without a goal. When those nights start going in, his season changes fast.
headline: Wyatt Johnston is owed some goals
